title: What can a charcoal mark date?
subtitle: Change a premise without changing the observation.
summary: Compare an excavation account with a later preservation experiment. Toggle three hypothetical premises to separate a conditional lower bound, a transferable analogy and an exact event date.
audience: Readers learning how material evidence supports a historical inference.
scope: A bounded reasoning exercise from selected reported observations. No exact eruption day, ancient inscription year or numerical survival probability is established.

passages.title: E1 · p.11
passages.text: The earlier account links a day/month inscription, renovation context and fragility to an autumn date. The reported date has no year; other words have competing readings.
passages.context: Prepared source summary, not an independent field observation or epigraphic transcription.

passages.title: M1 · p.5
passages.text: On 17 October 2023, oak charcoal was applied to ancient plaster on the same wall, at about 180 cm.
passages.context: Prepared source summary, not an independent field observation or epigraphic transcription.

passages.title: M2 · pp.5–6
passages.text: Temporary roofing excluded rain; intermittent sunlight, wind and rising damp remained. Three brief coverings were reported.
passages.context: Prepared source summary, not an independent field observation or epigraphic transcription.

passages.title: M3 · pp.7–8; figures 4–5
passages.text: Photographs used a color reference; twelve dates are listed. Figure 4 includes 24 August 2024; figure 5 ends at 17 August.
passages.context: Prepared source summary, not an independent field observation or epigraphic transcription.

passages.title: M4 · p.8
passages.text: Authors report continued legibility, with pressure-dependent differences and slight fading.
passages.context: Prepared source summary, not an independent field observation or epigraphic transcription.

passages.title: M5 · pp.9–10; figures 6–8; captions p.32
passages.text: Separate removal trials tested dry/wet methods and simulated rain; deliberate removal differs from passive survival.
passages.context: Prepared source summary, not an independent field observation or epigraphic transcription.

passages.title: M6 · pp.6,11–17,23–25
passages.text: Environmental comparability and interrupted renovation are author interpretations. Conclusions allow an earlier inscription year without establishing the eruption day.

claims.text: A month/day without an anchored year does not yield a dated calendar lower bound.
claims.qualification: The date must also refer to creating the mark, not merely an event the mark mentions.

claims.text: A modern survival observation supports its tested setting; a historical analogy needs additional premises.
claims.qualification: Neither a universal charcoal lifetime nor a frequency estimate follows.

context: Separate the reported date, renovation context and interpretation of fragility. The inscription date as reported has no year.
The modern experiment applied oak charcoal on 17 October 2023 to ancient plaster on the same wall. Temporary roofing excluded rain; other environmental exposures remained.
The listed photographic series and a selected paired comparison cover different sets of dates. One pair is not the entire observation schedule.
Deliberate removal trials and passive survival observations are different interventions. Do not combine them into one lifetime measurement.
A newer research announcement was found, but its underlying paper was inaccessible. This exercise does not claim to settle that newer work or the full scholarly chronology debate.
reviewLimitations: Selected source summaries and original conditional reasoning. No field experiment, specialist language review or participant observation is claimed.

Assume the mark precedes the destruction being considered and remains in its original context.
Any independent-year toggle is hypothetical; this dossier does not establish that year.
